rows.note: This is the all-purpose verb for giving someone a reward or incentive.

example.english: The company gave us a paid day off to reward us.
example.traditional: 公司獎勵咗我哋一日有薪假。
example.jyutping: gung1 si1 zoeng2 lai6 zo2 ngo5 dei6 jat1 jat6 jau5 san1 gaa3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for something given to reward someone for doing something well, whether or not it is money.

example.english: Employees who do well will receive a reward.
example.traditional: 做得好嘅員工會有獎勵。
example.jyutping: zou6 dak1 hou2 ge3 jyun4 gung1 wui5 jau5 zoeng2 lai6

rows.note: Use this for a cash reward, especially money promised for finding or catching someone.

example.english: The police have put up a cash reward of one hundred thousand dollars for catching the thief.
example.traditional: 警方出咗十萬蚊賞金，捉到賊就有錢攞。
example.jyutping: ging2 fong1 ceot1 zo2 sap6 maan6 man1 soeng2 gam1 zuk1 dou2 caak6 zau6 jau5 cin2 lo2

rows.note: Use this for money paid in return for carrying out a service or act rather than as a prize.

example.english: After the service is completed, the company will pay the reward stipulated in the contract.
example.traditional: 完成服務後，公司會按合約支付酬金。
example.jyutping: jyun4 sing4 fuk6 mou6 hau6 gung1 si1 wui5 on3 hap6 joek3 zi1 fu6 cau4 gam1
